chunks: From him, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: 'Do not make (anyone) swear by other than Allah.' And he said: 'Make the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian swear by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.يُحْلَفْ: to make swear / administer an oath

ai.seo_question: How should one administer an oath to Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential principle that the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) should be sworn in by Allah alone, rather than their own deities, to ensure the validity of the oath within an Islamic context. It reflects the Shia scholarly view on maintaining theological consistency while engaging with non-Muslims in legal or evidentiary matters, emphasizing the supremacy of the Divine Name. This practice aligns with the broader Islamic tradition of using the most universal and authoritative name for oaths to guarantee their binding nature.
